cf.title: Extension security improvement: Add support for extensions with an owned schema

input.subject: Extension security improvement: Add support for extensions with an owned schema

verdict_reasoning: The goal has shown demand and committer support, and no surviving objection is fatal. The decisive open point is replication-ondisk-1: on v12 a prerequisite installed into an owned schema gives a dump that does not restore and a pg_upgrade that loses a pg_depend row. security-1, maintenance-fit-2 and standards-compat-2 are fixable design points that need a decision from someone who knows extension dependencies and pg_dump. Only 3 of 43 messages were read directly, so confidence is medium.

brief.title: Extensions with an owned schema via an owned_schema control file option
brief.problem: Extension scripts run by CREATE EXTENSION and ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE use a search_path that contains the extension schema. If a less privileged user can create functions or operators in that schema, unqualified references in the script can resolve to them and run as superuser. Managed services that run these commands as superuser for their users are the main case.
brief.proposed_design: A new control file option owned_schema = true makes CREATE EXTENSION create the schema itself, and the command fails if the schema already exists. The schema becomes a member of the extension, so DROP EXTENSION ... CASCADE drops it. ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA renames the owned schema to a name that must not exist yet.
user_visible_surface: Control file option owned_schema (boolean, default false).
CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA: the named schema must not exist when owned_schema is true.
ALTER EXTENSION ... SET SCHEMA renames the owned schema instead of moving objects.
pg_dump output and a changed binary_upgrade_create_empty_extension signature in pg_upgrade support.
author_claims: Extension authors get a safe search_path without schema-qualifying every function and operator in their scripts.
SECURITY DEFINER functions can safely set search_path to the extension's owned schema.
The option removes the need for the pg_cron workaround of schema = pg_catalog plus create schema, and users still choose the schema name.
It helps avoid name conflicts between extensions.
The feature is useful even if only new extensions can use it.
brief.thread_state: The latest patch is v12, which also adds a check that fails test_pg_dump on any pg_dump warning. Rui Zhao reported a three-object dependency cycle through CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA ... CASCADE that breaks restore and loses a dependency in pg_upgrade, plus doc gaps; no reply yet.
unclear: Existing extensions have no migration path to owned_schema; the author only suggests catalog changes in their update scripts.
The proposal does not say how to handle extensions in a shared schema that requires another extension, the cycle Rui Zhao reported.
Comments on the owned schema are lost on dump and restore; the thread does not say which fix is planned.
No decision on whether to block ALTER SCHEMA OWNER TO, or other roles creating objects, in the owned schema.
No decision on making owned_schema the default.
search_queries: CREATE EXTENSION schema must not exist

objections.title: Owned schema shared via CASCADE breaks restore and pg_upgrade drops a dependency
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs CREATE EXTENSION os_owned SCHEMA shared_schema CASCADE, which installs the required os_base into the owned schema as well. The plain or directory dump then emits os_owned before os_base, so restore fails with "required extension is not installed". pg_upgrade reports success, but pg_depend no longer records that os_owned depends on os_base.
objections.argument: Message #43 shows this on v12, and nobody has replied. The v12 fix for the two-object loop in message #41 drops one edge from the dump sort, so any longer cycle through the owned schema is still unhandled. A silent loss of a pg_depend row in binary upgrade is the worst outcome, because no error appears and later DROP or ALTER EXTENSION acts on the wrong dependency graph. The proposal does not yet say whether to forbid this layout or to support it.
objections.author_must_show: Will CREATE EXTENSION reject a prerequisite extension landing in an owned schema, or will pg_dump and binary upgrade keep every pg_depend edge for this layout?

critic.reasoning: Message #43 gives a reproducer on v12 for a dump that does not restore and a pg_upgrade that loses a pg_depend row. No reply exists, and the proposal does not choose between rejecting the layout and supporting it.

objections.title: Safe search_path claim fails when a required extension sits in a writable schema
objections.failure_scenario: Extension X sets owned_schema = true and requires hstore, which is installed in public or in another schema where an application role has CREATE. That role creates an overloaded operator there. The control plane runs CREATE EXTENSION X as superuser, an unqualified operator in X's script resolves to the planted one, and the role becomes superuser.
objections.argument: The extension script's search_path also includes the schemas of required extensions, and owned_schema does not make those schemas safe. The v4 docs say that with an owned schema "the search_path now only contains trusted schemas" and that general-purpose SQL is "safe by default". In message #21 the author answers that the dependency can harden its own scripts, but that does not protect unqualified names in the dependent extension's script. Message #18 raised the transitive case, and the docs still state the guarantee without this limit.
objections.author_must_show: What keeps an owned_schema extension's script safe when a required extension lives in a schema that less privileged roles can write to, and do the docs state this limit?

critic.reasoning: CREATE EXTENSION adds the schemas of required extensions to the script's search_path, so an overload planted there still wins. Message #21 answers only for the dependency's own scripts, and the shown docs say the path "only contains trusted schemas".

objections.title: ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA flips its precondition per control file
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA script runs create schema app_ext followed by alter extension e set schema app_ext, which is the documented pattern today. For an owned_schema extension the second command fails because app_ext exists. The DBA cannot see from the command which behaviour applies without reading the control file or pg_extension.extownedschema.
objections.argument: Message #4 confirms that for owned schemas the command renames the schema and requires the target to be absent, which is the opposite of the existing rule. The same verb now has two contracts, and a flag the installing user did not choose selects between them. A committer would likely ask whether a rename is better exposed as its own form, or whether SET SCHEMA should keep its contract and report when the extension owns its schema. Message #43 shows the docs still describe only the old behaviour.
objections.author_must_show: Why should one ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA command require an existing schema for some extensions and a new one for others, and not use a separate rename form?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 confirms that SET SCHEMA requires an absent target for owned schemas and an existing one otherwise. Message #43 shows the ALTER EXTENSION docs still describe only the old rule, and the thread gives no reason for reusing the verb.

objections.title: Schema comment survives pg_upgrade but is lost on dump/restore
objections.failure_scenario: A user adds a comment on the extension's owned schema and moves the database with pg_dump and pg_restore. The comment is gone in the new database. The same cluster upgraded with pg_upgrade keeps it, so the two migration paths give different results.
objections.argument: Message #42 shows the ACL is dumped but the COMMENT is not, because the schema is now an extension member. A schema comment that survived a dump before this patch no longer does. The thread does not say which fix is planned.
objections.author_must_show: Will pg_dump emit the owned schema's comment as it does its ACL, so dump/restore and pg_upgrade give the same result?

critic.reasoning: Message #42 measured it: a schema comment that survived dump and restore before the patch is lost, while pg_upgrade keeps it. The loss follows the existing rule for extension members, but the thread has no answer on which fix is planned.

objections.title: Two permanent models of extension schema, with no path between them
objections.failure_scenario: An author of an existing extension such as pg_cron sets owned_schema = true in a new release. Clusters that already have the extension installed keep the old layout, because the control file option is read only at CREATE EXTENSION. The author either keeps both layouts or writes direct catalog updates in the update script, which pg_dump and pg_upgrade must then handle correctly.
objections.argument: Message #16 says the feature serves only new extensions, and the only migration route it offers is direct catalog changes in update scripts. pg_extension.extownedschema, the changed signature of binary_upgrade_create_empty_extension, and two meanings of ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA (move objects, or rename the schema) all become permanent. Messages #4 and #21 already float making owned_schema the default, which would be a second compatibility break later. A committer would likely ask for the migration design before the format is fixed.
objections.author_must_show: How does an installed extension switch to an owned schema without direct catalog changes, and would that route need different catalog or dump support than v12?

critic.reasoning: Message #16 confirms installed extensions have no supported route and points to catalog changes in update scripts. Reading control file options only at CREATE EXTENSION is existing practice, which lowers the weight, but nobody has shown that a later migration fits the v12 catalog design.

refuted.title: Dump of a shared-schema CASCADE layout does not restore
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs create extension os_owned schema shared_schema cascade, and the required extension os_base lands in the same owned schema. pg_dump emits CREATE EXTENSION os_owned before os_base, so the restore stops with "required extension is not installed". pg_upgrade reports success but drops the os_owned to os_base dependency, and nobody sees it until a later DROP or update.
refuted.argument: Message #43 reports a three-object cycle that v12 does not break, with a reproducer, and nobody has answered yet. It is the second cycle found in pg_dump ordering after message #40, so the owned schema dependency still has unhandled shapes. Rui Zhao proposes two fixes with different user-visible contracts: reject the layout at DDL time, or support it in dump and binary upgrade. The proposal does not yet pick one.
refuted.author_must_show: Will CREATE EXTENSION reject a prerequisite installed into an owned schema, or will dump and binary upgrade reproduce that layout and keep its dependencies?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which describes the same message #43 cycle and also states the pg_depend loss in binary upgrade.

refuted.title: Direct ALTER SCHEMA on the owned schema has no defined behaviour
refuted.failure_scenario: An admin runs alter schema ext_schema owner to app_role on an owned schema. app_role can then create functions there. The next ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE, run as superuser by a managed service, puts that schema on search_path, which is the attack the feature exists to prevent.
refuted.argument: Message #32 says changing the owner breaks the feature's core assumption and leans toward blocking ALTER SCHEMA OWNER TO, and message #35 prefers no special restrictions, but the brief lists the question as undecided. The proposal does not say what ALTER SCHEMA RENAME, OWNER TO or DROP SCHEMA do when the schema is an extension member. The safety claim in the extend.sgml hunk depends on these answers.
refuted.author_must_show: What happens on ALTER SCHEMA OWNER TO, RENAME and DROP SCHEMA for an owned schema, and how does the safe search_path guarantee still hold after each?

critic.reasoning: Messages #35 and #36 settle on no special restrictions, so normal schema rules apply, and Postgres already refuses a direct drop of an extension member. The scenario needs an admin to hand the schema to an untrusted role, which the thread weighed.

refuted.title: Catalog migration to owned_schema is left to hand edits in update scripts
refuted.failure_scenario: An existing extension wants owned_schema, so its update script updates pg_extension.extownedschema and adds a pg_depend row by hand. If the schema has a different owner or holds foreign objects, the flag claims a guarantee that does not hold. pg_dump and pg_upgrade then treat the schema as an extension member, and the user finds out on restore or on DROP EXTENSION ... CASCADE.
refuted.argument: Message #16 says existing extensions can only switch through "manual catalog hackery in its extension update script". The same message names two preconditions: the extension owner owns the schema, and the schema holds only extension objects. Nothing checks these when the flag is set by hand. A new pg_extension column whose only migration path is direct catalog writes puts its invariants into each extension's scripts, outside core.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the patch give one supported command that converts an installed extension and checks schema ownership and contents, so update scripts never write extownedschema directly?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on an extension author writing direct catalog updates, which a superuser update script can do today with the same risks. The patch does not add or document that route; the missing migration path is covered by maintenance-fit-2.

refuted.title: Making the schema an extension member drops its comment from dumps
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA comments on an extension's owned schema and later moves the database with pg_dump and restore. The comment is gone after restore, but a same-version pg_upgrade keeps it. The two upgrade paths produce different catalogs, and the DBA notices only when the documentation in the comment is missing.
refuted.argument: Message #42 confirms that the owned schema's ACL survives a dump but its COMMENT is not dumped. Before this patch the schema was an ordinary object, so its comment survived dump and restore. Turning a schema into an extension member changes which of its properties pg_dump keeps. The thread does not yet say whether security labels, ownership and other per-schema state follow the ACL rule or the member rule.
refuted.author_must_show: Which per-schema properties (comment, security label, owner, default privileges) does pg_dump preserve for an owned schema, and do dump/restore and pg_upgrade agree on all of them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-4. The added points on security labels and default privileges have no evidence in the thread.

refuted.title: Documented SECURITY DEFINER safety depends on schema ACLs nothing enforces
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA runs grant all on schema ext_schema to app instead of grant usage, as message #32 describes. The app role creates an overload in the owned schema. A SECURITY DEFINER function with search_path set to that schema, which the docs call generally safe, then runs the planted code as its owner, and nothing warns anyone.
refuted.argument: The v4 docs say it is "generally safe" to set a SECURITY DEFINER function's search_path to the owned schema. But message #36 keeps owned schemas open to normal GRANT and CREATE rules, following message #35. Message #32 calls the GRANT ALL mistake easy to make and suggests blocking ALTER SCHEMA OWNER TO, and the brief lists that as undecided. The guarantee holds only while the schema ACL stays untouched, and the docs do not say so.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the patch block CREATE grants and ALTER SCHEMA OWNER TO on an owned schema, or will the docs say the SECURITY DEFINER guarantee holds only while the schema ACL is untouched?

critic.reasoning: Messages #24 to #36 weighed this case, and a committer concluded in #33 and #35 that it is not a security issue and needs no special restriction. A grant of CREATE on any schema that holds SECURITY DEFINER functions carries the same risk today.

refuted.title: An extension that owns its schema adds dependency cycles that pg_dump and pg_upgrade do not handle
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs CREATE EXTENSION os_owned SCHEMA shared_schema CASCADE, and the prerequisite extension lands in the owned schema. pg_dump emits the two CREATE EXTENSION commands in the wrong order, so the restore fails. pg_upgrade reports success but drops the dependency of os_owned on os_base, and nobody notices until a later DROP or update.
refuted.argument: The patch makes a schema a member of the extension that lives in it, a dependency shape pg_dump never had before. Reviewers have found three separate faults from it: the two-object loop (message #40), the comment on the owned schema lost on restore (message #42), and the three-object cycle through requires (message #43), which is still open. The warning check in v12-0001 catches loops only for cases the tests exercise. Each later change to extension dumping or binary upgrade has to keep this case in mind, and a silently lost pg_depend row does not fail loudly.
refuted.author_must_show: Which rule rules out every cycle between an owned schema and other extensions, and does pg_upgrade check that it keeps every pg_depend row of an extension?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 for the open cycle and of standards-compat-4 for the comment. The two-object loop is fixed in v12, and v12-0001 makes test_pg_dump fail on any pg_dump warning.

refuted.title: Most of the protection is already available through the pg_cron control file idiom
refuted.failure_scenario: The project adds pg_extension.extownedschema, a new pg_upgrade support signature and special pg_dump ordering. Since then, reviewers have found a dump that does not restore and a pg_upgrade that silently loses an extension dependency (message #43). Extension authors who already use schema = pg_catalog plus CREATE SCHEMA gain only a schema name the user can choose.
refuted.argument: An extension with schema = pg_catalog and relocatable = false, whose script runs CREATE SCHEMA without IF NOT EXISTS, already gets a fresh schema owned by the installing role. The schema becomes an extension member, so DROP EXTENSION removes it, and functions can safely use SET search_path to that schema (messages #1, #2). Messages #1 and #4 say the idiom is a hack, fixes the schema name and does not allow relocation. That is a convenience gap, and a committer would likely ask whether it justifies a second mechanism with its own catalog, dump and upgrade cost.
refuted.author_must_show: Besides a user-chosen schema name and SET SCHEMA, what safety property does owned_schema give that the schema = pg_catalog plus CREATE SCHEMA idiom cannot?

critic.reasoning: The idiom cannot give a user-chosen schema name or relocation, and message #2 says it works by disabling extension schemas. An extension developer and three committers (messages #2, #7, #12, #15) support the need, so the gap is more than one author's convenience.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the signature of binary_upgrade_create_empty_extension, and message #43 reports a lost pg_depend row after pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the column pg_extension.extownedschema and makes the schema a member of the extension.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the control file option owned_schema for extension authors and changes src/include/commands/extension.h.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA and ALTER EXTENSION ... SET SCHEMA change their precondition when owned_schema is true.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump must order the owned schema and its extension; message #43 shows a dump that does not restore.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The feature exists to keep less privileged roles out of the search_path of extension scripts run as superuser.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every later change to extension dumping or binary upgrade must handle a schema that is an extension member.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will CREATE EXTENSION reject a prerequisite extension that lands in an owned schema, or will pg_dump and binary upgrade keep every pg_depend row for that layout?
What keeps an owned_schema extension's script safe when a required extension lives in a schema that less privileged roles can write to, and will the docs state this limit?
How does an installed extension switch to an owned schema without direct catalog changes, and does that route fit the v12 catalog and dump design?
Why should ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA require an absent schema for owned_schema extensions and an existing one otherwise, and not use a separate rename form?
Will pg_dump emit the comment on an owned schema as it emits its ACL, so that dump and restore match pg_upgrade?

committability.owner_note: Committers took part in the design discussion (messages #7, #12, #23, #30), but none has said they will commit it. The owner needs to know extension dependencies, pg_dump ordering and binary upgrade.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent pg_extension column, a second meaning of ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA, and correct pg_dump and pg_upgrade handling of a schema that is an extension member.
committability.author_follow_up: The author reached v12 and moved the entry between CommitFests himself until February 2026. Message #43 has no reply yet.

priority.reason: Extension authors and managed services need this, as message #2 describes, and costs fall only on extension DDL, pg_dump and pg_upgrade. The open cycle from message #43 and the search_path of required extensions need a design decision before more code review.

provisional_note: No code was read, and only 3 of 43 messages were shown directly. Whether v12's pg_dump ordering and binary upgrade handle all dependency shapes of an owned schema cannot be judged from the prose.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent extension creation in temporary schemas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first made create extension fail when the target schema is a temporary schema, as alter extension set schema already does. After objections, the author dropped that and changed psql's \dx and \dx+ to hide extensions in other sessions' temporary schemas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Chris Travers objected that other objects such as types can already be created in temporary schemas, so blocking extensions only would add another special case. The author dropped the block and kept only the \dx and \dx+ fix, which Chris Travers marked Ready for Committer. The author then found that a second session cannot create an extension already created in another session's temporary schema, but \dx no longer lists it. He returned the patch because it does not solve the root problem and makes things more confusing.
matched_queries: CREATE EXTENSION schema must not exist
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch as it stands does not actually solve the root problem and
makes things a bit confusing, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow excluding pg_temp or pg_catalog from search_path.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds special search_path entries "!pg_temp" and "!pg_catalog" that stop Postgres from searching pg_temp or pg_catalog implicitly, as a safety option for functions. It also warns when a user creates a schema with one of these special names, such as "$user".
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author doubted the feature's value without his separate SEARCH clause proposal, which did not gain support, because users would have to type "!pg_temp" by hand and pg_temp is already ignored for function and operator lookup. The reviewer agreed it was not worth adding without that main use case, and the author withdrew the entry. Earlier review comments also noted that the names need quoting and that "!pg_temp" is ignored when pg_temp is listed explicitly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I thought it sounded generally useful, but if we're not going to proceed
with the primary use-case for this feature, then perhaps it's not worth
going through this particular one-way door at this time.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix search_path for maintenance commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" while ANALYZE, CLUSTER, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW run as the table owner. This makes the commands behave the same for every caller and keeps a role with the MAINTAIN privilege from using search_path to gain the table owner's privileges.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis withdrew the patch after a reviewer reported that it no longer applied to HEAD, saying it was not yet clear this was the right change. He had already noted that it forces search_path in maintenance commands but not in other contexts, and that his broader proposals to fix search_path for functions got little agreement. Earlier concerns about breaking functions that depend on search_path were raised in messages not shown. Nathan Bossart supported committing it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am withdrawing this patch from the CF until it's more clear that this is what we really want to do.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checks on search_path for IMMUTABLE and SECURITY DEFINER functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Greg Stark proposed checks at function creation that warn or error when an IMMUTABLE or SECURITY DEFINER function has no search_path set, so that pg_restore failures and index corruption caused by search_path dependence are avoided. A later version instead filled in search_path in proconfig for the user, and he also floated a LEXICAL option modelled on SQL-standard function bodies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed a work in progress: it failed the regression tests, and the author raised open issues himself, namely cache flushes from a per-function search_path and the loss of inlining for functions with proconfig set. Andres Freund noted in October that it did not pass tests and asked whether the author planned further work and whether the entry wanted review. No reply from the author is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This currently obviously doesn't pass tests - are you planning to work on this
further?  As is I'm not really clear what the CF entry is for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for CREATE SCHEMA AUTHORIZATION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for create schema authorization and for the words after create schema <name>. Later versions also complete CURRENT_ROLE, CURRENT_USER and SESSION_USER for other commands that take a role, and merge the duplicated role list queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not post a new version after review comments in August 2021, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback in December. The open comments asked for comments on each role list query and for completion after create schema authorization <role>. Reviewers also pointed out that the patch offered SESSION_USER for create user mapping, where the syntax does not list it, and left out USER.
matched_queries: CREATE EXTENSION schema must not exist
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for more than a couple of weeks,
so I have marked it as returned with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add schema size information to \dn+
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Size column to psql's \dn+ output that shows the total on-disk size of the tables, materialized views and sequences in each schema. psql computes the size client-side with pg_total_relation_size(), for servers 8.1 and later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas noted that computing the size can take a long time on a big or busy database. Tom Lane asked whether \dn+ could fail or give misleading answers for users without permissions on some tables, and said the feature would block future tightening of access to size information. Julien Rouhaud noted that pg_total_relation_size() does no permission check at all. The author withdrew the patch and offered a server-side pg_schema_size() function as a possible alternative.
matched_queries: CREATE EXTENSION schema must not exist
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, even if
we allow people to get size info on tables they can't read today,
having this feature would be a roadblock to tightening that in
the future.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support % wildcard in extension upgrade script filenames
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension ship one update script with % as the old-version part of the filename, such as postgis--%--3.3.sql, to match any installed version. Postgres uses such a wildcard script only when no explicit update path exists, so PostGIS and similar extensions can stop installing hundreds of identical upgrade files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: vignesh C marked the entry returned with feedback in February 2024 because a regression test still failed in CFBot and the thread had no update. In August 2023 Daniel Gustafsson had returned an earlier entry because no patch applied and there was no consensus on a design. Robert Haas wrote then that Tom seemed opposed to any design that would solve the authors' problem, but Tom's messages are not among those shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With no update to the thread and the tests still failing I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adaptive query optimization: create extented statistics using auto_explain extension
precedents_retrieved.summary: Two patches: one lets the planner use extended (multicolumn) statistics when it estimates join selectivity, and one makes auto_explain create, or only suggest, CREATE STATISTICS for the columns of plan nodes where actual and estimated row counts differ beyond a threshold. The goal is to correct estimates for correlated columns without manual statistics creation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stalled after the patch stopped building in CI (auto_explain.c used ModifyTableState fields that no longer exist) and review comments were left open. Those comments, from Yugo NAGATA, asked for the reason behind each suggestion and reported redundant suggestions and duplicate ones that fail on pg_statistic_ext_name_index. The CF manager returned it with feedback; no design objection decided it.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposes extension-owned schemas; [P2], [P3], [P4] and [P6] cover search_path for maintenance commands and functions, and their recorded reasons do not apply here. Messages #8 and #10 link earlier search_path threads but report no rejection of this idea.
Not applicable; the objections above are fixable and concern dump round-trip and command contracts, not the goal itself.
Objections are limited to catalog, pg_dump and pg_upgrade state. The feature adds no WAL records or wire protocol changes and does not change the heap format.

Two fixable objections. The aim, keeping less privileged roles out of the schema used by superuser-run extension scripts, closes a real privilege escalation path that message #2 describes on managed services.

Hot-path cost is not a concern: the feature adds work only in extension DDL, pg_dump and pg_upgrade. Robert Haas reviewed the design (messages #23 and #30), but no committer has said they will commit it over 13 CommitFests.
One objection from this angle. Several reviewers support the direction and agree the user-chosen schema name is worth having, so this objection weighs less.

Demand is shown. In message #2 Marco Slot describes managed services where extension scripts were exploited to gain superuser, and treats the workaround as a hard requirement. Message #1 cites the pg_cron workaround, message #15 reports consensus, and Robert Haas agrees the problem is real in messages #7 and #12. The gain applies only to new extensions or new installs, which the author accepts in message #16, but that limits reach, not whether anyone needs it.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (maintenance-fit-2); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
